State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
Arte Digital World vs Sharada Sandip Kalokhe & Others on 4 March, 2015
Daily Order Goa State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission Panaji-Goa   First Appeal No. A/4/2015 (Arisen out of Order Dated in Case No. CC/5/2013 of District North Goa)   1. Arte Digital World Magnum Center, Next to Bread & More, M G Road, Panaji,Goa North Goa ...........Appellant(s) Versus 1. Sharada Sandip Kalokhe & others House No. 268, Manshe Bhat, Haliwada,Penha-de-Franca,Britona,Bardez,Goa North Goa 2. Idea Tele-systems Ltd. A-26/5, Mohan Co-op Industrial Estate, Mathura ROad New Delhi 110044 3. Huawel Technologies Co. Ltd. Huawel Industrial Base, Bantian, Longgang, Shenzhen 518129 Peoples Republic of China ...........Respondent(s)   BEFORE:     HONABLE MR. JUSTICE N.A.Britto PRESIDENT   For the Appellant: Adv. Shri. P. P. Singh   For the Respondent: ORDER
This appeal is filed by OP No. 1 in CC No. 5/13 and is directed against order dated 20/2/14, by which the Lr. District Forum has directed OP No. 1, the dealer, to refund to the Respondent No. 1/Complainant the full price of the handset with interest at the rate of 12% and compensation of Rs. 25,000/- and costs of Rs. 5000/-.
2.     Some facts are required to be stated to dispose off this appeal and for that the parties to this appeal are being referred to in the name as they appear in the cause title of the complaint.
3.     The complainant purchased from OP No. 1, on 29/3/12, a mobile handset known as Idea Smart Phone for Rs. 5,600/-.  The said handset was made in the People's Republic of China by OP No. 3 and imported to the Republic of India by OP No. 2.
4.     The handset had what is known as limited warranty subject to its terms and conditions.  The terms and conditions of the warranty were also reflected in the purchase voucher/tax invoice given to the complainant. The relevant terms and conditions can be reproduced and they are as follows:
This warranty of the Product extends for a period of 12 months for the Host unit, 6 months for Battery and Charger, and 3 months for Earphone commencing from the date of purchase as per retailer's bill/invoice date.
3.  Any defect arising due to misuse of the unit, damages due to liquid ingress, or physical abuse, or normal wear and tear will not be covered by this warranty.  Plastic components like front & back cover plus rubber component like key pads, antenna will not be treated under warranty coverage.
9.  Whether defective items or components are to be replaced or repaired shall be left to the sole discretion of Supplier.  In case of replacement of a part, the defective part removed from the unit becomes the property of Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd ('HUAWEI').
10. This Limited Warranty is your sole and exclusive remedy against HUAWEI and HUAWEI's sole and exclusive liability in respect of defects in your Product.  However, this Limited Warranty shall neither exclude nor limit to any of your legal (statutory) rights under the applicable national laws cr ii) any of your rights against the seller of the Product.
5.     A copy of warranty has now been produced on record by OP No. 1, at page 37 of the paper book.  Complainant confirms it is the same warranty which was issued to him at the time of purchase of the handset and further states that the same was shown by him/her to the Lr. District Forum.  We fail to understand as to why the Lr. advocate of OP Nos. 1 and 2 chose not to place the same on record before the District Forum, inspite of the fact that OP No. 2 was contesting the complaint.  Nothing had prevented of OP Nos. 1 and 2 to place the same on record to assist the Forum in coming to a just decision.
6.    The handset worked well for seven months until about 29/10/12, when according to the complainant, it started giving network problem and the complainant took it to OP No. 1 about three weeks later on 22/11/12 to address her grievances.  The complainant met a salesman by name Mr. Aman in the establishment of OP No. 1.
7. OP No. 1 is a firm of two partners and have their shop/establishment at Magnum Centre at Panaji.  For this Commission to know that OP No. 1 is firm of two partners, OP No. 1 had to go to the National Commission and return with order dated 3/12/14 in RP No. 2336/2014 and in that process make the complainant richer by Rs. 10,000/-.
8.     The complainant met one Mr. Aman on 22/11/12 in the said shop of OP No. 1 and the said Mr. Aman told the complainant and her husband that the said handset had to be sent to the service centre.  When the complainant requested the said Mr. Aman to give a receipt, for having received the handset, the said Mr. Aman refused and when the complainant told the said Mr. Aman and the salespersons that the complainant would be forced to lodge a cheating complaint against them with the police, one of the salesman made an endorsement on the purchase voucher/tax invoice that he had received the handset and called the complainant to collect the same after eight days.
9.    The complainant claims that on 30/11/12 when the complainant alongwith her husband went to collect the handset the said Mr. Aman told the complainant that there was a major fault in the handset and as such it was sent to the Company for replacement and the complainant and her husband were told to come on 7/12/12.
10.    The complainant claims that on 7/12/12 when the complainant with her husband went to OP No. 1 to collect the new handset, Mr. Aman told the complainant to come after two days to collect the new handset.  The complainant further claims that on 9/12/12 when the complainant phoned OP No. 1 and asked Mr. Aman about the new  handset,  Mr.  Aman  told  the  complainant to come and collect

 

 

 

 

 

the new handset and Mr. Aman told the complainant and her husband to come after another two days and when Mr. Aman was told that the complainant would lodged a cheating complaint with the police that Mr. Aman handed over the same mobile handset to the complainant and when the complainant and her husband reminded Mr. Aman that he had agreed to give a new mobile handset as replacement, Mr. Aman started behaving rudely with the complainant and her husband and told the complainant and her husband that the Company had repaired the old handset.
11.     The complainant claims that the repaired handset had a problem this time in that it become very hot and the complainant  feared that it would explode and so the complainant with her husband went to the shop on 14/12/12 and told Mr. Aman that the handset was getting hot and after checking Mr. Aman told the complainant and her husband that there was a major fault and defect and told them that the handset would be sent to the Company and will give the complainant a new handset as a replacement and that the complainant handed over the handset this time to Mr. Keith on 14/12/12 in the presence of Mr. Aman who assured the complainant and her husband that they would give a new handset as replacement and the said Mr. Keith made endorsement on the copy of the purchase receipt that he had received the handset for replacement.
12.    The complainant claims that on 22/12/12 when the complainant and her husband asked Mr. Keith about the handset, Mr. Keith told the complainant and her husband that he had received the new handset from the Company and further told the complainant and her husband to collect the new handset on 24/12/12  and  on  24/12/12 Mr. Keith told the complainant to come

 

 

 

 

 

on 26/12/12 since he was on leave and on 26/12/12 the complainant went to the police, as the complainant had no more faith and trust in Mr. Keith and Mr. Aman, and filed a police complaint.  To cut a long story short, Mr. Aman and Mr. Keith were called to the police station and subsequently on 18/01/13 the complaint was registered as an FIR under
Section 420
IPC against Mr. Keith, as an suspected accused.
13.     The complainant having filed a consumer complaint on or about 21/1/13 before the District Forum the same was contested by OP No. 2.  Although OP No. 1 and OP No. 2 were both represented by the same advocate, OP No. 1 chose not to contest the complaint by filing a written version and suffered an exparte order and thereafter chose not even to make any attempt to get the exparte order dated 28/06/13 set aside.
14.     The OP No. 2 in their written version took the plea that OP No. 2 was not in the business of manufacturing or repairing the handsets.  It pleaded that despite various requests made to the complainant to go to the authorized service centre at Margao, the complainant insisted for a new handset which is not as per the warranty.   OP No. 2 stated that the complainant had used the handset for a period of six months and suddenly started complaining about the same in the name of faulty handset.  OP No. 2 stated that the handset was under warranty and not under guaranty and therefore there was no question of any replacement as desired by the complainant and that under a warranty only a fault could be removed and there not be any replacement as alleged by the complainant and that the complainant was informed about the same that the complainant could approach the service centre at Margo for needful repairs.
15.     The case of the complainant is entirely based on the alleged promises made by Mr. Aman and Mr. Keith, from the shop of OP No. 1, for replacement of the handset, by the former on 30/11/12 and by the latter by endorsement on purchase receipt on 14/12/12.  The complainant seems to be conscious that in terms of the warranty the defective parts were required to be repaired or replaced (para 25 of the affidavit) but his entire case for replacement is based on what Mr. Aman and Mr. Keith allegedly told him.  The complainant had stated the following in his affidavit in evidence:
" Therefore when the entire set stops working or overheats and is defective, the Company is bound to furnish me a replacement for the handset and this is exactly what was explained to me by Mr. Aman and Mr. Keith."
"I say that I had never insisted for a new handset but was informed by Mr. Aman and Mr. Keith that I was entitled for a new handset."
16.     The Lr. District Forum has proceeded to accept the case of the complainant by observing that:
"7. We observe that the written promise of replacement was made by Shri. Keith in the premises of OP No. 1; in effect, in his own turf, on his own grounds. At least one colleague, the other employee, Shri. Aman was then present. May be other employees, office peon etc. were also around. We hence find it unlikely that complainant and her husband could force these employees of OP No. 1 in their own premises to write down such promise against their will. We hence conclude that the senior employee, Shri. Keith, made this promise in writing due to the fact that he recognized complainant as a genuine customer whose grievance it was his duty to resolve."
"9.     There is no doubt that is a supplier is willing and able to repair a defective product, Consumer Fora should not needlessly order replacement.  However, in the present instance, not only have Opposite Parties been incapable of rectifying the admittedly defective  instrument, but at least one i.e. Opposite Party-1, has exhibited a markedly obvious preference to intentionally harassing Complainant by making false promises and committing dates promising action but repeatedly failing to keep them."
17.     The Lr. District Forum has discharged OP No. 2 and 3 from any liability.
18.     Shri. P.P. Singh, the lr. advocate of OP No. 1, would submit that OP No. 1 is only a retailer and not an authorized service centre of OP No. 3, who has an authorized service centre at Margao.  Lr. advocate submits that when the complainant came to their shop on 22/11/12, the complainant was told to go to the service centre at Margao but the complainant forced the employees of OP No. 1 to take the handset and send the same to the service centre.  Lr. advocate submits that next time the complainant and her husband came with another complaint that the handset was getting hot and made a hungama in the shop of OP No. 1.  Lr. advocate submits that Mr. Keith is not an employee of OP No. 1 but of OP No. 2.  He submits that on 14/12/12 the complainant and her husband compelled Mr. Keith to take the handset and forced to make the said endorsement that the handset was received for replacement.
The lr. advocate submits that the handset is now with the  police and they have filed a charge sheet not only against Mr. Keith and Mr. Aman but also the two partners of OP No. 1 .  Lr. advocate submits that the said endorsement made by Mr. Keith has no value in the eyes of law as   it  was  made  under  pressure.   Lr.  advocate  submits  that   the

 

 

 

 

 

complainant did not examine any expert to show that the handset had a manufacturing defect and a bare statement of the complainant that the handset had a defect could not have been accepted, and, in this context Lr. Adv. Shri. P. P. Singh had placed reliance on The Commercial Officer, M/s. Piaggio Greaves Vehicle Pvt. Ltd., & anr. vs. Ramakant Samal, & ors., 2014 (4) CPR 75 as well as on
Chaitanya Educational Society vs. The Manager, Eicher Motors Ltd. & Ors.
, 2014 (4) CPR 624.  Lr. advocate submits that the complainants had not filed any income tax returns to show what business losses they had sustained.  Regarding the impugned order, lr. advocate submits that the same is based on presumptions and assumptions which cannot have a place in rule of law and the order was passed without any expert opinion.  Lr. advocate submits that Lr. District Forum was not right in referring to the dictionary to know the meaning of the word "warranty" when the same was available under
Section 12(3)
of the Sales of Goods Act, 1930, as amended and has placed reliance on Svenska Handelsbanken vs. M/s. Indian Charge Chrome and others, AIR 1994 SC 626.  Lr. advocate submits that the complainant cunningly did not produce the warranty card when the complainant was seeking reliefs on the basis of the warranty.  The lr. advocate submits that the complainant sought replacement of the handset but has been awarded refund of sale price, after using the handset for more than seven months.
19.     On the other hand Shri. Kalokhe, (complainant's representative and husband, complainant's alter ago, if we may use that expression) concedes that the warranty was not produced on record but the same was shown to the Lr. District Forum.  Shri. Kalokhe concedes that the handset worked for about six months and that  Mr. Keith  and Mr. Aman are the salesman of OP No. 1 and this

 

 

 

 

 

fact was conceded by Lr. Adv. Shri. P.P. Singh before the Lr. District Forum as reflected in para 5 of the impugned order.  Shri. Kalokhe concedes that on 22/11/12 Shri. Aman was reluctant to receive the handset but only when he was told that the complainant would give a police complaint for cheating that he accepted the same to be sent for repairs and on 30/11/12 Mr. Aman told him and the complainant that it was being sent to the Company for replacement.  Shri. Kalokhe submits that on 9/12/12 when the complainant and he went to collect the handset the said Mr. Aman was politely told that the police complaint would be lodged against him.  Shri. Kalokhe submits that on 14/12/12 Mr. Keith and Mr. Aman gave in writing that they had received the handset for replacement and as such they are bound to replace the same.  Shri. Kalokhe would submit that OP No. 1 was bound to replace the handset under vicarious liability of OP No. 3.
20.      There are certain misconceptions which need to be cleared before we proceed further.  Lr. District Forum was right in ignoring the decision of the National Commission dated 20/4/12 in R.P. No. 3780/2011 and the case of
General Manager, Telecom vs. M. Krishnan
and anr. on which it is based, as not applicable to the facts of this case. The case proceeded exparte against OP No. 1 and  therefore, the complaint has to be decided, and now the present appeal, on the basis of the evidence produced by the complainant and OP No. 2.  Mr. Keith and Mr. Aman were found in the establishment of OP No. 1 and the complainant was bound to infer that they are employees of OP No. 1 who made the said alleged promises/endorsement on 14/12/12.  OP No. 2 did not state in their written version or in the affidavit in evidence that they were their employees  but  on the contrary Shri. P.P. Singh, the lr advocate who

 

 

 

 

 

was then appearing for OP No. 1 and OP No. 2 before the District Forum made a statement that Mr. Keith was the employee of OP No. 1 which statement is recorded in para 5 of the impugned order.  It is not the case of Shri. P. P. Singh, the lr. advocate, that the said statement is wrongly recorded, and if that be so, lr. advocate ought to have taken steps to get the statement duly corrected. Only because Shri. P.P. Singh, the lr. advocate, now appears only for OP No. 1, it has become convenient  for him to submit that Mr. Keith is the employee of OP No. 2.  Mr. Aman and Mr. Keith are the employees of OP No. 1 with whom the complainant had dealings when the complainant alongwith her husband visited the establishment of OP No. 1.  However, only because the complaint proceeded exparte against OP No. 1, does not mean that the version given by the complainant has to be accepted lock, stock and barrel or as a gospel truth (see II 2009 CPJ 40).  Complainant's version cAN be accepted only in case it is found to be probable.  Complainant's husband was always alongwith the complainant but has chosen not to file any affidavit to support the case of the complainant, his wife.  It is well settled that only self serving statements of a complainant bereft of any material on record are not sufficient to establish deficiency in service (see Ashwani Kumar, 2009(1) CPR 420).
21.
Section 12(3)
of the Sales of Goods Act may provide that a warranty is a stipulation collateral to the main purpose of the contract, the breach of which gives a rise to a claim for damages but not to a right to reject the goods and treat the contract as repudiated, but we have
Section 14
of the C.P. Act, which enables a District Forum to direct an OP to remove the defects or to replace the goods or refund the price or to order payment of compensation as contemplated  therein.   This legal position has been taken note of by

 

 

 

 

 

the Apex Court in Indochem Electronic & anr. vs. Additional Collector of Custom, (I) 2006 CPJ (1) in the following words:
"27.  Although in terms of sub
section 3
of
section 12
no right accrues to a purchaser to reject the goods on breach of stipulation of warranty,  the same would not mean that the extent of damages cannot be equivalent to the price of the goods in as much as such a power has specifically been conferred upon the Commission."
22.   A warranty is the manufacture's or seller's promise to stand behind the product, and, in this case it was given by OP No. 3, the manufacturer, to the complainant.  A warranty is not one of the essentials of sale but it is collateral undertaking and in this case was given by the manufacturer, OP No. 3, to the complainant, to repair the defective items, but not to replace the whole handset, at its sole discretion.
23.     The complainant argued before the Lr. District Forum that OP No. 2 importer was vicariously liable for the acts of its dealer, OP No. 1.  The complainant now argues that OP No. 3 is vicariously liable for the acts of OP No. 1.  The expression "vicarious" means "done or suffered by one person on behalf of another".  The concept of vicarious liability ordinary arises in master and servant relationship where the master is held liable for the acts of his servants.  A manufacturer cannot be held liable for the acts of his dealer or retailer.  The complainant's case that the complainant did not insist for a new handset but was informed by the said Mr. Aman and Mr. Keith that he would be entitled for one because the handset was over heating is a story which cannot be accepted as gospel truth without any corroboration.  Moreover, such a story appears to be improbable as it opposed to the warranty conditions. The complainant  knew,  and  in  any  event  ought to have known that in

 

 

 

 

 

terms of the warranty, a defective unit alongwith the sales invoice was required to be brought or sent to the authorized service centre.  The endorsement made on the sales invoice on 22/11/12 clearly shows that the handset was received to be sent to the service centre.  The complainant accepted the handset duly repaired on 9/12/12 and there is nothing on record to say that the handset was not repaired. Subsequently, as per the complainant herself, the handset developed the problem of overheating and was again accepted to be sent to the authorized service centre on 14/12/12.  There is nothing on record to suggest that the handset was not repaired of the said overheating problem and OP No. 1 must have certainly got it back duly repaired by the service centre.  The complainant did not even find out whether it was working either on 22/12/12 or 24/12/12 before lodging the Police complaint on 26/12/12.  The Lr. District Forum observed, and in our view rightly, that if a supplier is willing and able to repair a defective product a consumer forum should not needlessly order replacement, but wrongly concluded, without any material on record, that the OPs were incapable of rectifying the defective instrument.  The facts on record clearly established that the handset had work well, without any problem for seven months and later, the two problems which it faced were attended to by OP No. 1 by sending it to the authorized service centre. We are inclined to believe that on both the occasions the handset was brought to OP No. 1, they had got it duly repaired, and this was as per the warranty given to the complainant by OP No. 3.
24.     The complainant and her husband are business people.  It is not their case that they did not know the scope of warranty given by OP No. 3.  It is also not their case that they did not know that as per terms  of  the  warranty  they  had to go either at Panaji or Margao to

 

 

 

 

 

the authorized service centre of OP No. 3.  Still they choose to go to the retailer, OP No. 1.
25.       In our view, the Lr. District Forum has entirely lost sight as to under  what  circumstances  the  so called promises or endorsements came to be made by the servants of OP No. 1, the said Mr. Aman and Mr. Keith.  On 22/11/12 when the complainant alongwith her husband went to the shop, they were told that it had to be sent to the service centre.  This was in conformity with the warranty.  Initially Mr. Aman refused to give a receipt but when threatened with filing a police complaint for cheating, the said Mr. Aman yielded and made an endorsement that he received the handset to be sent to the service centre.  Again, on 9/12/12 when the complainant and or her husband threatened Mr. Aman of lodging a cheating complaint that Mr. Aman handed over the repaired handset to the complainant.  The complainant would not have accepted a repaired handset on 9/12/12 in case the complainant was promised a replacement earlier.  Are we, therefore, to believe that Mr. Keith made the endorsement on 14/12/12 for replacement without any such threat from the complainant and/or her husband? Subsequently, the complainant indeed lodged a cheating complaint against Mr. Keith on 26/12/12.  If the complainant could get his way through on 22/11/12 and 9/12/12 by threats of filing police complaints for cheating, the only inference is that the complainant also got his way through on 14/12/12 by making a similar threat, or otherwise Mr. Keith would not have accepted the handset for replacement contrary to the warranty given to the handset. The probabilities of the case clearly suggest that replacement was promised by Mr, Keith out of fear of being implicated in a false criminal complaint of cheating and in  such  a  situation  the  said endorsement made on 14/12/12 is not

 

 

 

 

 

binding on Mr. Keith and much less on OP No. 1. Secondly, no retailer or dealer would have accepted the handset for replacement when  the  liability,  if  any,  for repair or for replacement, if at all, was that OP No.3, the manufacturer, and the manufacturer in terms had agreed for such replacement.  As already stated the warranty was only for repair, not for replacement.  Suffice to state that the said Mr. Keith had also no authority from OP No. 1 to receive the handset for replacement, in as much as OP No. 1 had also no authority to receive the same on behalf of OP No. 3, for replacement.  The said endorsement dated 14/12/12  in  the  circumstances  does  not at all appear to have been out of free will but out of coercion issued by the complainant and/or her husband to lodge a police complaint for cheating which was eventually lodged on 26/12/12 even without ascertaining whether the handset was duly repaired of its heating problem.
26.     Lastly, we may observe that the handset had worked well for seven months or more without any defect.  It would not have worked, if it had manufacturing defect.  Complainant had not examined any expert to prove that it had any manufacturing defect.  When the handset had network problem it was got repaired by OP No. 1 and handed over to the complainant on 9/12/12.  When the handset developed problem of overheating, the same was got repaired again.  The complainant and/or her husband did not even try to find out whether it was repaired or not but went and filed police complaint for cheating against the said Mr. Keith on 26/12/12.  OP No. 1 had tried to help the complainant, as a dealer, although the complainant was required to approach the authorized service centre.  The Lr. District Forum therefore was also not right in passing  the  impugned  order  for  full refund, after the handset was

 

 

 

 

 

used for seven months, and compensation of Rs. 25,000/- which would have enabled the complainant to purchase 4 of such sets.
27.     In view of the above discussion we allow the appeal and set aside the impugned order and proceed to dismiss the complaint but considering the facts with no order as to costs.     [HONABLE MR. JUSTICE N.A.Britto] PRESIDENT
